target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.scope: global commercial-aviation accident census under IATA methodology
evidence.observation: IATA reports 11 fatal accidents and 523 onboard fatalities. Its fatal-event categories reconcile exactly to six fatal jet accidents and five fatal turboprop accidents. The six fatal jets are Saratov An-148 plus five Boeing events: Southwest B737, Cubana/Global Air B737, Fly Jamaica B757, Air Niugini B737 and Lion Air B737 MAX.

evidence.publisher: National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB), United States
evidence.observation: Boeing 737-7H4 N772SW, Southwest flight 1380, scheduled Part 121 passenger operation; one passenger fatality.

evidence.publisher: Instituto de Aeronáutica Civil de Cuba / accident investigation commission
evidence.scope: event-level; mirrored copy of identified authority report
evidence.observation: Boeing 737-201 XA-UHZ, commercial passenger flight DMJ 0972; 112 fatalities.
evidence.use: candidate authority evidence with public-host provenance caveat

evidence.publisher: Papua New Guinea Accident Investigation Commission (AIC)
evidence.authority_role: investigation authority after FSM Annex 13 delegation
evidence.observation: Scheduled passenger flight PX073, Boeing 737-8BK P2-PXE; one passenger fatality. AIC records serial number 33024.

evidence.publisher: Komite Nasional Keselamatan Transportasi (KNKT), Republic of Indonesia
evidence.observation: Scheduled passenger flight LNI610, Boeing 737-8 MAX PK-LQP, 189 persons onboard; all fatally injured.

evidence.publisher: Guyana Aircraft Accident & Incident Investigation Unit (GAAIIU)
evidence.authority_role: state accident-investigation authority; report copy hosted by JCAA
evidence.observation: Boeing 757-200 N524AT; the final authority report's injuries table classifies one passenger as a fatality. BSFM therefore follows the authority's fatal-injury classification rather than constructing a retrospective timing rule.
evidence.use: candidate authority and delayed-fatality taxonomy evidence

source_conflicts.resolution: retain AIC competent-authority value; preserve discrepancy for identity audit

completeness_assessment.reason: The IATA annual fatal-event categories exhaustively map the six fatal jets; five are Boeing and all five have event-level authority evidence. The delayed Fly Jamaica death is classified as fatal by the competent authority, and the P2-PXE identity discrepancy is preserved without changing membership.
